category_title: Confident student with articulation-based Spoken Language Disorder
scenario_title: Vocabulary application during peer talk with articulation difficulties
minimal_context: The student is participating in a turn-and-talk peer conversation about the book Rocket Writes a Story to answer a prompt about who inspires them.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We just finished reading Rocket Writes a Story. Now it is time for our turn and talk. Who is someone that inspires you?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'll start! I declared that I couldn’t sleep last night because I was thinking about this.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay. What did you think about?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I looked outside and I saw a bird perch on the end of a tree branch, and then I thought about my family.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: So, who is someone that inspires you?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: My sister. She sires [sic] me to get my homework done. My sister sires me [sic].

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: We just finished reading Rocket Writes a Story. Now it is time for our turn and talk. Who is someone that inspires you?

STUDENT: I'll start! I declared that I couldn’t sleep last night because I was thinking about this.

TUTOR: Okay. What did you think about?

STUDENT: I looked outside and I saw a bird perch on the end of a tree branch, and then I thought about my family.

TUTOR: So, who is someone that inspires you?

STUDENT: My sister. She sires [sic] me to get my homework done. My sister sires me [sic].

task.content: Responding to the prompt 'Who is someone that inspires you?' during peer talk about Rocket Writes a Story
task.learning_goal: Application of the words during peer discussions

context.environment: Kindergarten classroom during interactive read-aloud sessions
context.social_setting: Peer conversations / turn and talk to partners

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When using the explicitly taught vocabulary word 'inspires'
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Unable to pronounce it correctly; said 'She sires [sic] me to get my homework done. My sister sires me [sic].'
related_quotes: My sister. She sires [sic] me to get my homework done. My sister sires me [sic].

behavior_patterns.condition: When participating in peer conversations and using explicitly taught vocabulary words
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Demonstrated difficulty with articulation; could not articulate certain sounds in words, but took a leadership role, was the first to engage in peer talk, and consistently and accurately used novel words in context
related_quotes: I declared that I couldn’t sleep.
I saw a bird perch on the end of a tree branch.
